target_customer: Web hosting providers and sysadmins running Linux servers who want a control panel cheaper than cPanel
problem: Hosting control panels like cPanel and Plesk were costly and closed; Virtualmin offers an open source panel built on Webmin.
business_model: Open core: free GPL edition, paid Pro edition with support

founders.name: Jamie Cameron
founders.background_notes: Virtualmin about page: created Virtualmin, Webmin and Usermin; Webmin first released October 1997.

founders.name: Joe Cooper
previous_startups: Swell Technology, web-caching appliance vendor, 1999 to 2005
founders.background_notes: Per Virtualmin about and who pages.

technical_complexity.rationale: Managing Apache, mail, DNS and databases across distributions through Webmin modules is broad but standard sysadmin engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Installed servers and Webmin's large user base create lock-in, but open source code and strong incumbents limit pricing power.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it; Virtualmin remains a small independent company.

market_need_then: Shared hosting providers paid per-server licenses for cPanel or Plesk; the company reports over a thousand hosting providers using Virtualmin.

identity.logo: Logo in SVG and PNG in a press kit with usage rules

branding.brand_signature: The Webmin and Virtualmin open source pairing
branding.community_and_virality: Active forum on Discourse migrated from older forums; claims over 100,000 active Virtualmin installations (project README) and over 3 million Webmin downloads a year.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong niche community but a confusable compound name and little press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Virtualmin built on Webmin's existing open source base, took YC money in 2007, and became a durable small business serving over a thousand hosting providers. Its team stays tiny and independent, with releases continuing in 2026. It did not scale to venture size, a result consistent with an open core model against cPanel's entrenched position.
notes: Funding amount not public; the date 2007-01 comes from CB Insights and the YC investment from Virtualmin's own about page. Competitors: only post-2019 comparison articles found (cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin), nothing dated near the 2007 batch, so the list is empty. Founded 2005 per company. Location sources conflict (Austin, Mountain View).
